children.name: Murrayona phanolepis Kirkpatrick, 1910
children.description: Sponge subspherical, globular or slightly flattened (Fig. 11 A). Consistency hard and harsh to the touch. The exhalant region is covered with scales, except for the oscula (one or two), which are surrounded by sagittal triactines (Fig. 11 B). No scales are present in the inhalant region (Fig. 11 C). Surface smooth and translucid, allowing observation of the canals. Atrium reduced to spaces within the hypercalcified skeleton. Aquiferous system leuconoid. The skeleton can be divided into two regions: one superficial composed of free spicules (Fig. 11 B – E) and a basal skeleton with a framework of hypercalcified sclerodermites (Fig. 11 F). The inhalant region is marked by regular triactines surrounding the inhalant apertures (Fig. 11 C). On the exhalant region, there are scales covering the cortex (Fig. 11 D) and diapason in bundles underneath the scales (Fig. 11 E). Trichoxeas are present on the external surface and among the hypercalcified basal skeleton. Spicules (Fig. 12; Table 5) Oscular triactines: Sagittal. Actines cylindrical, undulated, with rounded tips. Paired actines much longer than the unpaired one (Fig. 12 A). Size (UFRJPOR 7525): 123.6 (± 24.2) / 7.9 (± 1.4) µm (paired); 27.7 (± 7.3) / 8.7 (± 1.6) µm (unpaired). Triactines: Subregular. Actines cylindrical, undulated and commonly curved, with blunt to rounded tips (Fig. 12 B). Size (UFRJPOR 7525): 117.2 (± 17.0) / 11.5 (± 2.7) µm. Scales: As the actines are fused, this spicule is almost circular.
